section.title: Activity
section.para: Use this information to answer questions 1 - 2.

blockquote.para: To help pay for his tuition, a college student plans to work in the evenings and on weekends. He has been offered two part-time jobs: working in the guest-services department at a hotel and waiting tables at a popular restaurant.

list.item: The job at the hotel pays $18 an hour and offers $33 in transportation allowance per month.

The job at the restaurant pays $7.50 an hour plus tips. The entire wait staff typically collects about $50 in tips each hour. Tips are divided equally among the 4 wait staff members who share a shift.

blockquote.para: The equation \( 7.50h + \frac {50}{4}h = 18h + 33 \) represents a possible constraint about a situation for 1 month.

list.item: Solve the equation and check your solution.
Add a scale on the number line so that the point marked with a circle represents the solution to the equation you found in question 1.

problem.para: When you have finished graphing, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.

list.item: Which job pays better if he works fewer hours than the solution you found in question 1?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample. The hotel job pays better if he works fewer than 16.5 hours a month because I found the pay for both jobs using numbers that are less than 16.5 and found that pay at the hotel job is always higher.

exercise.data-solution-options: ["Hotel Job", "Restaurant Job","The pay is the same."]

list.item: Which job pays better if he works more hours than the solution you found in question 1?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample. The restaurant job pays better if he works more than 16.5 hours a month because I found the pay for both jobs using numbers that are more than 16.5 and found that pay at the restaurant job is always higher.

problem.para: Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.

image.alt: A number line is shown with an open circle on a point in the middle. The number is shaded to the right of the open circle.

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples.

list.item: Inequality 1 shows the pay at the hotel \( (18h+33) \) being greater than the pay at the restaurant \( 7.50h+ \frac{50}{4} \). Earlier, we found out that the hotel job is better when the student works less than 16.5 hours. Graph B shows \( h<16.5 \). This means Graph B shows the solution to Inequality 1.

If we substitute a value greater than 16.5 for \( h \), we have a true statement for Inequality 2 and a false statement for Inequality 1. This means \( h>16.5 \) is a solution to Inequality 2 but not to Inequality 1.
If we substitute a value less than 16.5 for \( h \), we have a true statement for Inequality 1 but not for Inequality 2. So \( h<16.5 \) is a solution to Inequality 1.
